newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba sees 97/98 parent oper profit 145 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba sees 97/98 parent oper profit 145 bln yen.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Tuesday it forecast parent operating profit of 145 billion yen in the year to next March 31, up four percent from the previous year.
The major electronics maker also expects group operating profit to rise seven percent from a year earlier to 165 billion yen.
It also said it expects group sales of semiconductors to rise nine percent from a year earlier to 970 billion yen in 1997/98 after an 11 percent decline in the previous year.
Senior executive vice president Atsumi Uchiyama said the semiconductor division was in the red by a small amount last business year, but this fiscal year it was expected to return to the black.
He said the LCD division was also in the red last business year but that also was expected to return to the black this year.
Toshiba forecast group sales of LCDs of 135 billion yen in 1997/98, up 17 percent form a year earlier.
The company plans group capital investment on semiconductors of 150 billion yen in 1997/98, down 12 percent.
It also plans group capital investment on LCDs of 20 billion yen this business year, up 67 percent from a year earlier.
Toshiba plans overall group capital investment of 380 billion yen in 1997/98, up 11 percent. Its sees parent capital investment rising eight percent to 195 billion yen.
It forecast group sales of personal computers in 1997/98 would rise 49 percent from a year earlier to 1.1 trillion yen after an 80 percent year-on-year gain last business year.
Shipments of Toshiba PCs in Japan this business year are seen rising 42 percent to 850,000 units. Overseas shipments are seen rising 50 percent to 3.15 million units.
